clue.text: Two seconds into Michael Jackson song, strange kick

indicators.note: into says the two seconds go inside the song title

parts.note: Bad is a 1987 Michael Jackson hit
S is the abbreviation for second, so two of them make SS
rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A pop fan finds an odd thump a couple of seconds into a Michael Jackson track.
explanation.definitionFit: Drummers call the large pedal-operated drum of a kit the kick drum, so kick is its common nickname.

clue.text: Stick plug in this location

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, AD for short
in this location means here

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a plug: push it into this socket and it will stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or hold fast, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Odd characters in small-town social event

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the hyphenated word that follows

explanation.surface: Eccentric locals turn up at a village get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a gathering of guests, often literary or artistic, at a host's home.

clue.text: Moving? What, moving walls?

indicators.note: walls is a verb here: the stirring word encloses the request to repeat

parts.note: moving, in the sense of stirring the emotions, is rousing
eh? is what you say when you mean what? or pardon?

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a removal firm's talk asks whether moving means shifting the walls themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' looks like a noun being moved, but it is a verb: the stirring word walls in the request to repeat. 'moving' serves twice, as the definition's echo and as stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Being found a new home is moving house, so the question mark flags a sense of moving.

clue.text: Changing agent, as Greek character changing agent

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of agent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy who is turning sides is cast as a Greek in the cast list.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutagen is a substance that alters genetic material, literally an agent of change.

clue.text: Badger that man caught next to rock

parts.note: that man is he
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A bullying fellow was arrested beside a large boulder.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or bully them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fundamentalist group is obliged to imprison old lady

indicators.note: to imprison means the words for obliged hold the mother inside

parts.note: he has to go means he is obliged to go
old lady is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: A militant faction feels compelled to lock up an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palestinian Islamist organisation is a militant fundamentalist movement.

clue.text: One's part of the settled establishment: one's royalty

definitions.text: One's part of the settled establishment

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself a colon
one is I, and the 's adds S
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A snobbish insider boasts of belonging to the Establishment and to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the clue is not just punctuation: it supplies its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a member of an established colony, so one belonging to that settled body fits.

clue.text: Work's not started? Better to be hidden

indicators.note: not started tells us to lose the opening letter

parts.note: a job is work, and the 's adds S
better, recovered from illness, means cured

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to start a task thinks it wiser to lie low.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is concealed or covered from view.

clue.text: Sound of shot muffled in battle

indicators.note: sound of tells us the answer is said like the words that follow

parts.note: a shot or throw is a shy, and muffled is low, as a quiet voice

explanation.surface: A war story notes the dull report of gunfire in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiloh was an 1862 battle of the American Civil War in Tennessee.

clue.text: It seems rocks around lake to be permanent

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters sit round the lake's letter
rocks is a verb: the letters of it seems are shaken up

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Boulders round a lake look as though they will last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' turns IT SEEMS into TIMESES and 'around' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless is unaffected by the passing years, so lasting and permanent.

clue.text: Respirator I have switched on for ages? One switch needed!

indicators.note: one switch needed asks us to swap the two vowels in the phrase built

parts.note: a machine that has been switched on will run
for ages means for a long time, long

explanation.surface: A machine that has been running for ages needs to be turned off.
explanation.walkthrough: I RUN LONG has U then O; 'One switch needed!' swaps those two vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron lung was a large mechanical ventilator used for polio patients.

clue.text: Bad shilling not cut short

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

indicators.note: short drops the final letter

parts.note: not cut, as an unabridged text, is in full

explanation.surface: A dud coin is the one that was not clipped down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful conduct is wicked or wrong, a synonym for morally bad.

clue.text: Actor cut BBC series, 'Land Larks'

indicators.note: larks are pranks or capers, so the letters play about
cut means the broadcaster's initials lose their last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer axes a BBC programme about skylarks in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims BBC to BB, and 'Larks' shuffles BB, SERIES and LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The booming-voiced English performer starred in Flash Gordon and Z Cars.

clue.text: Supporter wants reason to protect old college

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear that supports

indicators.note: to protect means the words for reason enclose the old letter

parts.note: reason as in good judgment is sense

explanation.surface: A backer needs good grounds to save an ancient institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasenose is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Chap's dismay on breaking dresser

parts.note: a chap is a lad; the 's stands for has, joining it to the rest

indicators.note: breaking tells us the letters of dismay are broken up

explanation.surface: A man's alarm at smashing a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal attendant who helps a woman with her clothes literally dresses her.

clue.text: Forget about sarcastic VIP, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the words by how they are spoken

parts.note: a right toff is a scornful description of an upper-class bigwig

explanation.surface: Ignore the self-important celebrity's scornful remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh person; 'right' adds sarcastic emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something off is to dismiss it as lost or not worth pursuing.

clue.text: Some criminals call 24 in order to see 19 21

indicators.note: in says the criminals and the call go inside the word order

parts.note: a band of criminals is a gang

indicators.note: the answer to 24 means nearly, so the word for call is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them

explanation.surface: Crooks almost phone, in sequence, to watch a busker in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '24' (almost) acts as an indicator, trimming the call by one letter; '19 21' is the definition, a street musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A person cranking a barrel organ for coins is a classic busking street performer.

indicators.note: the answer to 10 read as two parts says without time, so the letter T for time goes

parts.note: something lasting for ever is undying, deathless

explanation.surface: A bare string of cross-references, reading as a numerical puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The second '10' is read literally as time-less: drop T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to 12 means wicked, a straightforward synonym for unethical behaviour.

clue.text: Sodium-taking leads to a sickness

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
taking a drug is using it, as in drug use

explanation.surface: Consuming too much salt brings on queasiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the feeling of wanting to vomit, a form of sickness.

clue.text: Urban engineers should have let it stand on the perimeter

indicators.note: on the perimeter means the instruction's letters form the boundary round the engineers

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning leave as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Town planners should have left the boundary alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Street used as an adjective, as in street style, means of the city or urban.

clue.text: Well oiled but unlikely to come loose

definitions.meaning: well oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk's knot that will not slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both drunk and firmly fixed, two common senses.

clue.text: As a player I am in such short supply

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
short means the word such loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A performer complains that work is scarce for people like them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SUCH to SUC; 'supply' shuffles I AM IN SUC.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician plays an instrument, so is a player.

clue.text: Climbing tree, he pondered the human condition

indicators.note: climbing in a down light means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: sumac is a shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: A philosopher up a tree contemplates the meaning of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus, the French writer of The Outsider, explored absurdity and the human situation.

clue.text: Someone who doesn't dream — not as before

definitions.meaning: read as two words: one who does not yearn, a person with no longing

explanation.surface: A realist who has given up their former fantasies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means not any more, and read cryptically names a person who does not long.

clue.text: As good as a spymaster in TV series

indicators.note: in places the spymaster inside the TV series

parts.note: Lost was an American TV drama about plane-crash survivors
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief appearing in a television drama is just as good.
explanation.definitionFit: As good as means nearly, a near-synonym phrase for virtually.

clue.text: Strike force vacated France when opening front

indicators.note: opening means the pieces open up the word for front and sit inside it

parts.note: to put on a front is to act
F is the international code for France

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving just the outside letters

explanation.surface: A military strike force pulls out of France as the front opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties force to its outer letters; France's letter goes first inside the act, before them, regardless of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone emotionally, as news strikes or moves you, is to affect them.

clue.text: Guide's frightful ordeal crossing 19

indicators.note: crossing means the shuffled letters straddle the road
frightful suggests the letters of ordeal are mangled

parts.note: the answer to 19 is abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A guide describes the dreadful experience of crossing a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges ordeal to LODEAR, and the cross-reference 19 stands for the street, shortened to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A star navigators steer by, especially the Pole Star, is a guide.
